literal: Shade and water are harmful if they cause harm; also the nature of relations will become harmful if they do harm.
translation: Even shade and water, though normally pleasant, are harmful if they cause illness; likewise, even the relationship of one's own kin becomes harmful if they act to cause harm.
modern: நிழலும் நீரும் உடலுக்கு நோய் போன்ற துன்பத்தைத் தருமானால் அவை தீமையானவையே; அதுபோல, நம் உறவினர்களின் தன்மையும் நமக்குத் துன்பம் தருவதாக இருந்தால் அது தீமையானதாகவே முடியும்.
explanation: The poet uses a beautiful analogy from nature to explain internal enmity. Shade and water are universally sought after for comfort, yet if they cause sickness, they are avoided as harmful. Similarly, one's own relatives and close associates are expected to offer support and comfort. However, if their character and actions bring harm or betrayal, that relationship becomes toxic and must be treated as dangerous. The word 'நீர்' is brilliantly used twice with different meanings: first as 'water' (paired with shade) and second as 'nature or character' (of relatives).
